habit_scope: Soil termiticide where termites are a potential problem, before the slab, do not disturb treated soil before the pour. ORNL §2.2 / Fig 2-4 / DECAY AND TERMITE checklist. AF&PA Protection Against Termites. CMHC termites are localized Canadian geography — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Not printed as 'Fontana yes / Utah no.' Gap gap-P06-fontana-utah-split. Do not trade treatment for shields (P05 D8).
how_it_is_done: ORNL: 'Techniques for controlling the entry of termites through residential foundations are advisable in much of the United States (see Figure 2-4). The following recommendations apply where termites are a potential problem. Consult with local building officials and codes for further details.' 'Treat soil with termiticide on all sites vulnerable to termites.' Checklist: 'Treat soil with termiticide, especially with insulated foundations.' 'Do not disturb treated soil prior to pouring concrete slab.'

Before treatment: 'Remove all roots, stumps, and scrap wood from the site before, during, and after construction, including wood stakes and formwork from the foundation area.' (ORNL). Same wood-out as habit prep.

ORNL: soil treatment is 'the most effective technique to control termites with an insulated foundation.' Termite shields are optional and 'should not be regarded as sufficient defense by themselves' (P05 D8). Restrictions on termiticides may make the option unavailable or substitute products more expensive / less effective — do not invent a product name. CLASS is termiticide.
AF&PA Protection Against Termites: soil treatment named with shields and clearances. Do not trade treatment for shields.

CMHC Ch1 Termites and Other Insects: present only in a few localized areas in southernmost BC, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba and Ontario; clearance 450 mm (18 in) unless wood is treated; foundation walls at least 150 mm (6 in) above ground; supports visible for mud tubes; metal or plastic barrier through insulation if it could conceal activity. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not copy Canadian termite geography as a US market split.
ORNL: 'in some regions termite control may be considered more critical than thermal considerations, while the reverse is true elsewhere.' That is not Fontana vs Utah. Gap gap-P06-fontana-utah-split.
Still do habit prep. Treatment is not a skip of poly or plumbing. Licensed applicator is not named in these books (same Gap as P05).
trades: ORNL: treat soil — applicator not named as licensed. No crew size.
tools_equipment: Not named beyond treating soil. Form stakes must come out before treatment/slab (ORNL).
inspection_hold_points: Soil treatment before slab where termites are a hazard (ORNL).
Do not disturb treated soil prior to pouring (ORNL).
Form wood / grade stakes / scrap out of the foundation area (ORNL).
Consult local building officials (ORNL). Confirm AHJ.
when_this_beats_habit: Where termites are a potential problem (ORNL: much of the United States; consult local officials). Not printed as Fontana-only.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Skipping treatment in a termite region because a shield is on the sill. Copying CMHC's Canadian termite map as a US market. Inventing Fontana-yes/Utah-no as a book fact (Gap).
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They skip pulling the form stakes and then they walk the treated dirt. ORNL says leave it alone until the truck pours.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Termite treatment where required belongs with the AHJ. Confirm with AHJ / local officials. Not a stamp. CMHC geography is Canadian — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
risk_if_swapped_late: Treating after the slab is not the pre-slab Method. Catch before the pour.
plain_language_summary: Where termites are a live issue, treat the soil before the slab and do not walk it after. Pull the form stakes and the scrap wood. A shield is not a cheaper skip of treatment. The books do not say Fontana yes / Utah no — that split is a Gap. CMHC's termite map is Canadian.
spanish_summary: Donde hay termitas, trate el suelo antes de la losa y no lo pise después. Saque estacas y sobrantes. El escudo no sustituye el tratamiento. El libro no dice Fontana sí / Utah no — es Gap. El mapa de CMHC es canadiense.

remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching, occupied-site, shoring, demo of an existing house) are not a sequence in CMHC/ORNL/HUD/FM — Gap, do not invent remodel-only methods. Essential Guide is framing-only (opened 2026-08-30; silent on site/layout). B&D Room Additions not used as a P00–P06 sequence.
labor_notes: Licensed applicator for termiticide is not named in these books (same as P05). Crew Gap.
layering: Roots/stumps/scrap/form wood out → treat soil → do not disturb treated soil → poly/gravel/plumbing as habit → pour.
code_to_check: Consult local building officials and codes (ORNL). Confirm with AHJ. CMHC termite geography is Canadian / NBC — not IRC. Do not invent IRC R318.
time_money: ORNL: termiticide restrictions may make substitutes more expensive / less effective — no dollars printed. Shields are not a cheaper skip.

inspector_looks_for: Treated soil undisturbed before the pour (ORNL).
Roots, stumps, scrap, form wood gone (ORNL).
Shields not accepted as a substitute for treatment (ORNL; P05 D8).
inspector_fails: Disturbing treated soil before the pour (ORNL: 'Do not disturb treated soil prior to pouring concrete slab').
Leaving wood stakes and formwork in the foundation area (ORNL termite).
common_messups: Relying on termite shields alone (ORNL: not sufficient defense by themselves).
Leaving scrap wood and form stakes for termites to eat (ORNL).
do_not_cheap: Soil treatment where termites are a hazard, especially with insulated foundations (ORNL hold).
Do not disturb treated soil before the pour (hold).
Do not trade treatment for shields (P05 D8 / ORNL).
Wood out of the foundation area (hold).
